stories.title: An Anthropic mathematician says Claude helped prove the Riemann hypothesis, and mathematicians are still checking
stories.deck: Levent Alpöge says an unreleased version of Claude helped him produce a machine-checkable proof of mathematics' most famous open problem, but verification will take time.
summary: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician who works at Anthropic, said on Friday that he used an unreleased version of the company's Claude AI model over roughly six weeks to build a proof of the Riemann hypothesis. The problem, posed by Bernhard Riemann in 1859, concerns how prime numbers are spread along the number line and is often called the most famous unsolved question in mathematics. This is a claim by the author and his employer, not an established result.

According to the BBC, the proof runs to more than 250,000 lines written in Lean, a programming language that lets a computer check each logical step of a proof. TechCrunch adds that colleagues, including MIT's Andrew Sutherland, have confirmed that the Lean code compiles. That is significant, because it means the formal argument holds together inside the checker. It does not yet mean that people understand why it works, and Alpöge reportedly had no human-readable explanation to hand at first.

Alpöge acknowledged the awkward timing, coming a day after Anthropic's stock market debut. He told the BBC that he messaged chief executive Dario Amodei on Sunday to ask about announcing the result, called the timing "horrible", and said he took responsibility for not being able to wait. He denied any cynical intent.

Specialists are cautious. Terence Tao said on Friday that digesting the work will take time, though a living author can answer questions. TechCrunch reports a separate, human-only proof of the generalised Riemann hypothesis, shared by Stanford's Ravi Vakil and credited to postdoctoral researcher Alessandro Masullo after about twelve years of work. That draft has not been written in Lean, so its validity is also unconfirmed.

The announcement follows other AI-lab claims in mathematics, including an OpenAI Navier-Stokes claim that remains unconfirmed. A group of mathematicians has warned that using headline problems to market products harms the discipline. Expect months of scrutiny before anyone can call this settled.

stories.title: GTA VI makes $3.79 billion on its first day, Rockstar says, far above early analyst estimates
stories.deck: Rockstar's long-awaited game went on sale worldwide on Thursday; the company's own figure tops outside estimates of about $2.4 billion.
summary: Grand Theft Auto VI went on sale worldwide on Thursday 19 November after a wait of about thirteen years since its predecessor, and Rockstar Games now says it earned $3.79 billion in its first day, which it calls a new record for entertainment in any medium. The Verge reports that the company, in an announcement through parent Take-Two, also said it sold 32.5 million pre-order copies. Those are company figures and have not been independently audited.

The BBC's account, written before Rockstar's number emerged, shows how far outside estimates fell short. Sensor Tower, which draws on email receipts and public gaming profiles, put first-day sales and pre-orders at more than 24.5 million copies, worth about $2.36 billion, with roughly three quarters on PlayStation 5 and the rest on Xbox. Niko Partners projected worldwide sales above $3 billion this year. The game is believed to have cost more than $1 billion to make.

Network data told the same story. Cloudflare said PlayStation 5 downloads in the UK ran at 8.6 times normal, and that overall online traffic peaked at 11.2 times normal in Australia, 9.3 times on the US East Coast and seven times in Britain. Virgin Media O2 said the game's 212GB install file broke its evening traffic record. Some players apparently switched console regions to start early.

There are limits. The game has been censored in Japan over graphic content and has not been approved for sale in mainland China. Rockstar has not given a PC release date or a timetable for multiplayer expansion. Critics have been warm, and IGN called it an "uncompromisingly engineered" masterpiece. Whether the pace holds beyond the launch rush is the next question.

stories.title: Tech sell-off pushes the S&P 500 and Dow into correction as Anthropic gives back half its debut gain
stories.deck: A rout in AI-linked shares sent the Nasdaq down 5.3% on Friday, and Anthropic closed near its $83 offer price.
summary: US stocks fell sharply on Friday as a sell-off in technology shares spread across global markets. The BBC reports that the Nasdaq dropped 5.3%, the S&P 500 lost 3.7% and the Dow fell 1.9%. The S&P 500 and the Dow are now more than 10% below their recent highs, the usual definition of a correction, though all three indexes are still up on the year. Markets in Europe and Asia also fell, and Taiwan had its worst weekly decline since 1990.

Anthropic, which listed on the Nasdaq on Thursday, gave back about half of its first-day gain. After opening at $111.50 and closing Thursday at $97.17, up 17%, the shares fell 8.5% on Friday to close near $85, only slightly above the $83 offer price. Analysts had warned that early swings were likely because Anthropic is the first frontier AI company to list, so there are no direct comparisons to anchor its valuation.

The BBC links the broader fall to worries about the scale and speed of AI spending, which has topped $1 trillion over the past year, and to political uncertainty after Democratic gains in the early-November midterms raised doubts about future support for the industry. Company-specific news added to the pressure. Nvidia fell 13.7% on unconfirmed Reuters reports of an SEC inquiry into its accounting. Tesla and SpaceX each lost more than 7.6%, Meta fell over 4% and Amazon over 5%.

AlphaSense strategist Ed Moya said the IPO had failed to restore broad confidence in AI and that investors are asking what growth costs, with Wall Street shifting toward demanding profit and cash flow. That is one analyst's reading rather than a settled explanation, and one-day moves of this size can reverse quickly.

stories.title: Trump threatens a 'tremendous tax' or ban on US firms building AI data centres overseas
stories.deck: The president floated the idea after returning from Asia, but said his own team was hearing it for the first time, so its status as policy is unclear.
summary: President Donald Trump said on Friday that he intends to stop American technology companies from building artificial intelligence data centres abroad, warning of a heavy financial penalty for any that do. Speaking to reporters after his return from Asia, he said cabinet members were learning of the plan at the same moment as everyone else. The BBC notes that he gave little detail, so it is not clear whether this will become formal policy or how it would be enforced.

Trump argued that keeping the buildings in the United States is needed to stop China from capturing the benefits of what he called super intelligence. Data centres house the servers and chips that run services such as ChatGPT and Claude, and they have become a political issue at home. The BBC cites Pew Research Center figures of about 3,000 US facilities as of April, with another 1,500 in approval or construction.

Local objections to electricity use and noise helped Democratic candidates who favour tighter rules win elections on 3 November, according to the report. Trump, for his part, urged communities to treat the sites as assets rather than block them.

He pointed to Google's €13 billion plan, announced in September, for three AI data centres in Finland. Construction of two was paused last month after objections to forest clearance, and Trump said his administration would stop the project. Canada has been pitching itself as a friendlier host with less local resistance. Google was contacted for comment. Until a proposal, legal basis or tax rate is published, the threat remains a statement of intent.

stories.title: Bending Spoons buys Mailchimp from Intuit for $3.68 billion, less than a third of the 2021 price
stories.deck: The Italian app group is paying about $3.68 billion for the email marketing platform that Intuit bought for roughly $12 billion five years ago.
summary: Italian software company Bending Spoons has agreed to buy the email marketing platform Mailchimp from Intuit for $3.68 billion, TechCrunch reports. Intuit paid around $12 billion for the business in 2021, so the sale price is well under a third of that. The deal fits Bending Spoons' pattern of buying established, late-stage internet products and running them itself.

Intuit's shares have fallen sharply over the past year as investors worry about competition in business software and from artificial intelligence. The company told Reuters that selling Mailchimp lets it concentrate on AI tools for small businesses, and that the proceeds will go toward share buybacks.

There is a detail that complicates the headline. Bending Spoons described the purchase as all-cash, but TechCrunch notes that Intuit is at the same time buying $368 million of newly issued Bending Spoons shares. That makes the net deal roughly 90% cash and 10% stock.

Bending Spoons co-founder and chief product officer Matteo Danieli told TechCrunch in a July interview that the company sees itself as an operator that improves well-known brands. Mailchimp's history may follow it into the new ownership: its 2021 sale caused controversy because employees reportedly received no equity or sale proceeds, after the founders had allegedly promised they would never sell. No integration plans, job cuts or pricing changes were reported in the coverage.

stories.title: California's attorney general subpoenas Nvidia over its former chief's ties to China
stories.deck: Rob Bonta says Nvidia and Jensen Huang's conduct raises red flags about possible investor deception and access to restricted chips.
summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta has issued an investigative subpoena to Nvidia, TechCrunch reports, adding a state inquiry to the growing scrutiny of the chip maker after Jensen Huang's resignation. The state wants to know whether Nvidia or Huang helped China obtain restricted high-performance graphics chips or sensitive information, and whether shareholders and the public were misled about those exposures.

Bonta said the conduct of Nvidia and its former chief executive raises "bright red flags", including about the ways in which the company may have misled investors. The subpoena is an information request, not a finding of wrongdoing.

The background, as TechCrunch tells it, is that Huang stepped down last week after disclosures about a relationship with Alice Huang, whom US officials suspect of working as a Chinese spy, and about other relationships with staff. Nvidia, Huang and the other people named have not confirmed the reporting on internal relationships, and the extent of Alice Huang's alleged government links is still being examined by US authorities.

Other pressure is building. Congressional committees are pursuing a subpoena for Huang, who has agreed to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving on 26 November. The SEC is reported to be conducting a civil inquiry into public disclosures, and Democratic lawmakers have started their own review of how the previous administration handled chip sales to China. Nvidia's board chair has said the company has no plans to bring Huang back, despite calls from Elon Musk and others for his return.

stories.title: Tens of thousands of UK fridges were quietly secured from hackers in a secret nationwide operation
stories.deck: After a flaw was found in widely used refrigeration controllers, officials and engineers raced to take devices off the internet before attackers could exploit them.
summary: A hidden effort across Britain has protected tens of thousands of commercial fridges and freezers from hackers, the BBC's Joe Tidy reports. In late October, refrigeration consultants at Omega Solutions found a serious weakness in popular controllers made by the British company Resource Data Management, known as RDM. The controllers let operators manage dozens of cooling units remotely and are used by supermarkets, warehouses, restaurants, petrol stations and stadiums.

Security firm Pen Test Partners confirmed and extended the finding. Its Ken Munro said the controllers had a weak-password problem like that seen in attacks elsewhere in Europe, and that criminals or state-backed hackers were probably days from working it out. The National Cyber Security Centre, the environment department and the Food Standards Agency organised industry calls. Thousands of devices were taken off the open internet, either remotely or in person.

The urgency came from recent history. The BBC lists three waves of fridge-hacking this year: in August against US military bases, on 11 and 12 October against hundreds of sites in France using Danfoss systems, and on 1 and 2 November against dozens of supermarkets in seven European countries. France blamed Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps for the October attacks, and Iran called that baseless. Two Russian hacktivist groups have made unverified claims that the BBC says should be treated with caution.

RDM disputes how serious the flaws were. Chief executive Ged Evans said exploiting them required physical hardware and a test environment, that comparisons with the European attacks are unfair, and that there was no sign of malicious activity on its controllers. The company says it moved quickly to issue patches and contact customers.

stories.title: India's festive-season smartphone sales fall 22% as memory costs push prices up
stories.deck: Counterpoint Research says shallow discounts and dearer handsets left buyers relying on easy credit, and Apple saw a double-digit dip.
summary: Smartphone sales in India fell 22% year on year during the festive season from 8 October to 10 November, according to Counterpoint Research figures reported by the Economic Times. The research firm blames weaker consumer demand and higher device prices, driven by rising costs of DRAM and NAND memory chips.

Samsung stayed on top with a 21% share despite an 8% sales decline, followed by Vivo with 18% and Oppo with 12%. Apple's sales dropped by double digits even with the launch of the iPhone 18 series. Separate data from CyberMedia for the third quarter showed shipments down 20% overall, with Xiaomi down 28%, Vivo and Oppo down 25% and Apple down 16%. Note that the CyberMedia numbers cover a different period from the festive window.

Higher component costs left brands little room to discount. Festive price cuts were 10% to 25%, compared with 35% to 40% last year, so entry-level phones stayed expensive. Brands leaned on no-cost EMIs, bank offers and trade-ins, and 48% of sales were finance-led. Brands in the sub-Rs 20,000 segment fell by nearly 50%, while newer names such as Ai+ grew online, selling more than a million units. Online visits did not turn into purchases, and stores saw slow footfall.

Counterpoint analyst Shubham Singh said price increases stopped promotions from driving big volumes, and that buyers purchased out of need, often on EMIs, or kept their current phones. The figures are preliminary post-festival checks, and a separate Counterpoint forecast cited by the paper expects flagship prices to rise more than 30% by year-end.

stories.title: SpiceJet gets a DGCA show-cause notice as its fleet shrinks below ten aircraft
stories.deck: The aviation regulator cites mass cancellations, unpaid dues and the lack of a credible plan to return grounded aircraft to service.
summary: India's aviation regulator, the Directorate General of Civil Aviation, has issued a show-cause notice to SpiceJet over widespread flight cancellations and delays, unpaid liabilities and what it sees as a failure to present a workable plan to bring grounded aircraft back, the Indian Express reports. The notice is dated 17 November, and the airline was given seven days to reply or face orders without a hearing.

The numbers are stark. Civil aviation ministry data from 19 November put SpiceJet's on-time performance at 25%, and tracking data showed that more than half of its recent flights were cancelled. The report says the operating fleet has fallen below ten aircraft because lessors cannot be paid, and that domestic market share dropped to 0.6% in October, from about 4% in January and roughly 15% in 2019.

Debts have pushed vendors, airports and oil companies to put the airline on daily cash-and-carry terms. Foreign authorities have also warned the DGCA about disruption on international routes from late payments. In one example, Dubai Airports halted check-in services over unpaid dues. The regulator is also concerned about insurance renewals, and about whether SpiceJet meets the rule that airlines flying international routes must deploy at least 20 aircraft or 20% of capacity domestically.

SpiceJet's board has approved raising up to Rs 5,500 crore to repair its finances, but the Indian Express says the timing of that fundraising is unclear. The details come from ministry data, airport and tracking sources and people familiar with the matter. SpiceJet's own response to the notice was not part of the report.

stories.title: Nikhil Gupta gets more than 19 years in US prison over plot to kill Sikh separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun
stories.deck: A New York judge sentenced the Indian national to 235 months; India denies any role and calls Pannun a terrorist.
summary: A US federal judge in Manhattan has sentenced Indian national Nikhil Gupta to 235 months, a little over 19 years, in prison for his part in a failed plan to assassinate Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, the BBC reports. Gupta pleaded guilty in February to murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire and conspiracy to commit money laundering. The judge indicated he will probably be deported after serving his term.

US prosecutors say that Gupta was recruited in May 2023 by an Indian intelligence officer named Vikash Yadav, who allegedly supplied Pannun's New York address and daily routine. Pannun is a US citizen and a spokesman for Sikhs for Justice, a group that campaigns for a Sikh homeland called Khalistan. Gupta unknowingly approached a US government informant, who introduced him to an undercover Drug Enforcement Administration agent posing as a hitman. He was arrested at Prague airport in June 2023 and extradited. Prosecutors also say he told the undercover agent that Hardeep Singh Nijjar was another target, and that there were "so many targets".

The Indian government denies involvement and describes Pannun as a terrorist, a label he rejects. Pannun told the BBC the guilty plea confirms that the Modi government planned an assassination on American soil. These are his claims and those of US prosecutors, and India disputes them. Former US attorney Jay Clayton said Gupta believed he could target someone over free speech without consequences.

The case is linked to the 2023 killing of Nijjar outside a temple in British Columbia. Then Canadian prime minister Justin Trudeau said in September 2023 that there were credible allegations tying India to it, which India also denies. Sikh community figures in Canada told the BBC that the sentence was the first sign of justice for Sikhs.

stories.title: Congress sweeps Rajasthan's rural polls and says the BJP government's end has begun
stories.deck: Counting for district and block councils gave Congress boards in most of the councils declared, including a string of defeats for BJP-linked families.
summary: Congress has won a decisive victory over the ruling BJP in Rajasthan's village-level elections, according to results reported by the Indian Express. Of 37 Zila Parishads, the district-level councils, whose results were declared, Congress formed boards in 25 and the BJP in nine, with one going to others and two hung. In the 419 Panchayat Samitis, the block-level bodies, Congress formed boards in 269 of the 418 declared, the BJP in 73 and others in 63.

In Jaipur's Zila Parishad, Congress took 41 of 57 wards, the BJP 12 and the Rashtriya Loktantrik Party two. Zila Pramukh Rama Chopra and deputy Mohan Dagar both lost. The paper's list of upsets includes the wife and both sons of minister Jhabar Singh Kharra, who lost in Sikar by 51 votes, as well as relatives of a Congress MLA, a police official and BJP leaders. Some relatives of prominent figures did win, including the son and daughter-in-law of BJP leader Rajendra Rathore.

Rajasthan Congress chief Govind Singh Dotasra said on X that the landslide shows the BJP government has lost public trust after three years, calling it a rebuke from villagers, farmers, youth and workers. He said the countdown to the end of the government has begun. That is a party leader's political reading. Local council elections are often driven by local candidates and caste arithmetic, and they do not map neatly onto state or national results.

The tallies come from figures on the Election Commission site for declared results. A few councils had no clear majority or were won by smaller parties, including the RLP. The BJP had not issued a detailed response in the coverage reviewed.

stories.title: Eleven die and about 180 are hospitalised after toxic liquor in Manipur's Chandel district
stories.deck: Authorities are testing to confirm the cause as the toll rises over three days; police say the drink came from Kakching district.
summary: At least 11 people have died in three days after drinking suspected spurious liquor in Manipur's Chandel district, and roughly 200 others needed hospital treatment, the Indian Express reports. The first two deaths were reported on 18 November, and the toll had reached 11 by Friday as more people fell ill. Patients are being treated at hospitals in Imphal. NDTV puts those hospitalised at 181.

Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh visited a hospital on Friday to review the situation. The Chandel Superintendent of Police said the drink was bought at Sugnu in neighbouring Kakching district rather than made in Chandel. He stressed that traditional wine is not brewed in Chandel and warned against linking the deaths to local production.

The Deputy Commissioner said medical and scientific tests are under way to determine the cause, and issued an advisory while health and police teams carry out investigation and prevention work. The cause of death has not been officially confirmed, though district officials have connected the deaths to drinking alcohol. The Hindu reports that the district administration has also warned residents.

Toxic liquor deaths in India are usually blamed on methanol, an industrial alcohol that is sometimes added to illicit drinks, but no such finding has been announced here. Until laboratory results are out, the numbers and the source of the drink should be treated as provisional.

stories.title: Cyclone Akvan makes landfall near Gopalpur with no deaths reported, after 3.72 lakh evacuated
stories.deck: Heavy rain flooded streets in Ganjam district, and 41 trains were cancelled, but officials reported no casualties or damage to public infrastructure.
summary: Cyclonic Storm Akvan crossed the coast near Gopalpur in Odisha on Friday morning, bringing heavy rain to southern Odisha and northern Andhra Pradesh, the Indian Express reports. Winds were sustained at 70 to 80 km/h with gusts up to 90 km/h. Ganjam district received nearly 200 mm of rain in 24 hours, and streets flooded in towns including Berhampur and Digapahandi. The Hindu later reported that the system weakened into a depression with no major damage or flood threat.

Odisha Chief Secretary Anu Garg said there were no deaths and no damage to public infrastructure. Municipal teams were pumping out standing water. Authorities had moved more than 3.72 lakh people out of vulnerable areas before landfall, and 4,470 pregnant women were shifted to health facilities, where more than 1,400 deliveries have taken place. The Rushikulya and Bahuda river basins were being closely watched, and no problems were reported.

Schools, beaches and tourist sites were closed as a precaution. The railways cancelled at least 41 trains, including a Vande Bharat service, and rescheduled several others. Forecasters said the system would move north-north-east and fade into a deep depression while spreading rain to other districts, and the Hindu says monsoon-type rain will resume over Tamil Nadu.

The all-clear is limited. Officials flagged localised urban flooding and said rivers remain under watch. The no-casualty statement is the state's own account at the time of reporting, and damage assessments for farms and housing usually take days.

stories.title: Nepal's prime minister Balen Shah arrives in Delhi for his first bilateral visit abroad
stories.deck: The two-day trip, with talks with Narendra Modi on 23 November, follows early friction between Kathmandu and New Delhi.
summary: Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah arrives in India on Saturday for a two-day visit that marks his first bilateral trip abroad since taking office in March, the Indian Express reports. The agenda covers trade, development partnerships, energy, water, physical and digital connectivity, technology, innovation and sports. The Times of India notes that a rail link tying the birthplaces associated with Ram and Sita is among the connectivity themes.

India's Ministry of External Affairs said Prime Minister Narendra Modi will hold talks with Shah on 23 November to review the full range of ties and exchange views on regional and international issues. The ministry described the visit as a sign of continuing high-level contact and of India's "Neighbourhood First" policy. Nepal's Foreign Ministry called it an opportunity to examine the partnership "through a forward-looking lens".

The paper adds some background. Shah took power on 27 March after student-led protests forced out KP Sharma Oli's government. Relations were strained afterwards because Shah said he would not travel abroad for a year and would meet only heads of state or government, which led to the cancellation of a visit by Indian Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri and blocked attempts by the US ambassador.

The ice has since thawed. Nepal's finance minister visited India in September, ruling-party figure Rabi Lamichhane went to New Delhi in June, and Shah thanked India for flood relief in early September. The outcome of the talks is not yet known, and the BBC has run a separate analysis calling the trip a test of the relationship.

stories.title: Britain and the EU agree a deal on food exports, carbon markets and youth mobility
stories.deck: Prime Minister Andy Burnham says the UK will explore even closer ties, while the Conservatives and Reform call the agreement a bad bargain.
summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham struck a deal with the European Union in Brussels on Friday covering food exports, emissions trading and youth mobility, and said the UK will explore even closer ties. Legislation is expected in Parliament next week. The BBC reports that most checks on British food exports to the EU would end by 2028, in return for the UK following certain EU rules, and that the two sides will link their emissions trading systems by 2028.

A youth experience scheme would let up to 100,000 people aged 18 to 31 from each side travel, work and study for up to three years, starting by January 2030. Talks on tuition fees stay open for six months. Police forces will share more data to counter people smuggling and trafficking.

Burnham called it a good day and cited Treasury projections of a £17 billion boost to GDP, up to 0.5%. He said the government will publish a ten-year plan next month, and that its manifesto limits rule out rejoining the single market or customs union or accepting free movement. European Council President António Costa said the EU remains open to the closest possible relationship. Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called the summit a turning point.

The opposition is sharply critical. Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said the deal is unfair, that farmers will follow foreign rules and that arriving young people will compete with domestic job-seekers, and she disputed the £17 billion figure, saying existing modelling shows 0.0%. Reform's Nigel Farage called it a betrayal. Liberal Democrat leader Ed Davey said it amounts to tweaks. The BBC's Faisal Islam separately cautions that the deal does not guarantee lower prices.

stories.title: A Russian missile and drone land in Poland during a Western military exercise, and Warsaw calls it a provocation
stories.deck: Nobody was hurt, but Poland's prime minister says the incursion was deliberate, and NATO's chief is due in Warsaw on Saturday.
summary: Poland said on Friday that three objects entered its airspace during a large Russian aerial attack on Ukraine: a Kh-101 cruise missile, a second suspected missile and a jet-powered drone. The BBC reports that the Kh-101 landed in a rural area at Nowy Lipowiec, about 50 km from the Ukrainian border, at around 06:30 local time. The other missile came down near Rudnik nad Sanem, and the drone crashed near Mołodycz. There were no injuries or damage.

Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the incursion was deliberate because it happened during Western military exercises in the region. The UK- and France-led "Koalicja 2026" drill in south-eastern Poland involves 11 nations of the Coalition of the Willing, and the objects fell near the Nowa Dęba training area. Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz called it a Russian provocation and said Poland would seek more NATO help. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte condemned the violations, said NATO jets were scrambled and planned to visit Warsaw on Saturday.

UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting called it a provocation meant to divide Europe and weaken support for Ukraine, and British Prime Minister Andy Burnham called it unacceptable. Russia has made no public comment. Intent is Warsaw's assessment. Previous spillovers have occurred, including a 2022 incident in which two Polish farmers died.

The strike came the same day as Russian attacks that killed at least eight people across Kyiv's Dnipro bridges and a Lviv station, after Vladimir Putin's threats over the Kerch Strait bridge. Moldova also reported a brief drone violation on Friday.

stories.title: Formula 1 bosses agree to bring back V8 engines from 2030
stories.deck: A 2.1-litre turbo hybrid with a smaller electric element would replace the current V6 units, aimed at lower cost and better racing.
summary: Formula 1 leaders have agreed to introduce V8 turbo hybrid engines in 2030, replacing the current, widely criticised power units, the BBC reports. The sport's governing statement on Friday said manufacturers had backed the plan, which keeps advanced sustainable fuels but aims for engines that are lighter, simpler and cheaper. The new units will be 2.1-litre turbocharged V8s, two cylinders more than the current 1.6-litre V6 layout.

The electrical side shrinks to a maximum of 200 kW, split evenly between always-available power and an overtake mode. That addresses driver complaints that today's cars run short of battery energy and race in an artificial way. Total output is expected to reach roughly 1,050 bhp in overtake mode and more than 900 bhp otherwise. Other targets include a 150 kg power-unit weight limit, an annual engine budget cap of $190 million and a car weighing under 700 kg without fuel.

General Motors will delay its own Cadillac engine until 2030, give up its current voting rights and use Ferrari customer engines through 2029. FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem called the deal a major milestone. McLaren's Zak Brown said everyone is excited. Cadillac chief Dan Towriss noted the team already has a V6 base to develop a V8 from.

Fans should not expect the thunder of the 2006 to 2013 V8 era, which the BBC says will not return because of commercial risks for city-centre races such as Miami and Las Vegas. Some details remain unresolved, and Fernando Alonso has already said he will not stay for the V8 era.

stories.title: Russell fastest in Las Vegas final practice after a clash with Verstappen at Turn 14
stories.deck: The Mercedes driver topped the only dry session by 0.9 seconds, while stewards are due to review his contact with the Red Bull.
summary: George Russell led the final practice session for the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Friday, Autosport reports, after both Thursday sessions were wrecked by rain. It was the only dry running of the weekend, but the 6.2 km street circuit was cold at about 14°C and grip was poor. Many drivers chose soft tyres to build heat and slid into escape roads.

Russell's best lap was 1m34.041s. Kimi Antonelli was second, 0.911s back, followed by Lando Norris, Charles Leclerc and Franco Colapinto. Max Verstappen was sixth, 1.309s off, after a sideways moment and steering rack trouble. Liam Lawson, Lewis Hamilton, Pierre Gasly and Arvid Lindblad completed the top ten. Autosport also notes that Russell chose not to take a Mercedes turbo upgrade, to avoid grid penalties.

The session ended in drama. Russell passed Verstappen at Turn 14 and the two made side-on contact that forced the Red Bull off the track. Russell said "fun and games" on team radio, and the incident is set to be looked at by the stewards. Earlier, Norris cheered over radio when Verstappen locked up, saying "instant karma", after being annoyed at being forced past by the Dutchman.

Isack Hadjar asked for a penalty for Williams' Alex Albon over a near miss. Because the other sessions were wet, practice running was not representative, so qualifying could still reshuffle the order.

stories.title: KL Rahul becomes the first Indian opener to score Test hundreds in all four SENA countries
stories.deck: His unbeaten 100 in Wellington completes centuries in South Africa, England, Australia and New Zealand.
summary: KL Rahul scored an unbeaten century on day three of the first Test against New Zealand in Wellington, making him the first Indian opener, and only the second Asian opener after Pakistan's Saeed Anwar, to score Test hundreds in all four SENA countries: South Africa, England, Australia and New Zealand. The Indian Express says he reached the mark off 207 balls after lunch at the Basin Reserve.

He shared the opening stand with Yashasvi Jaiswal, who made 85 off 89 balls. It was Rahul's twelfth Test hundred as an opener, which equals Murali Vijay and puts him behind only Sunil Gavaskar with 33 and Virender Sehwag with 22. He is the fourth Indian opener to score a Test hundred in New Zealand, after Gavaskar, Gautam Gambhir and Shikhar Dhawan.

At 34, Rahul has four hundreds in 21 innings in the current World Test Championship cycle and has gone past captain Shubman Gill as India's leading run-scorer. His earlier SENA hundreds were 110 in Australia in 2014, four in England (149, 129, 137 and 100), and 123 in South Africa in 2023.

The report, from the paper's sports desk, includes no direct quotes. Selection remains a talking point, though: former players criticised India's decision to leave Mohammed Siraj out of the Wellington Test.

stories.title: Surat–Bilimora stretch of the Mumbai–Ahmedabad bullet train line to be energised, with a first service targeted for 15 August 2027
stories.deck: Railways say the 50 km elevated section gets live overhead power on 20 November; the India-built B28 train is meant to run at 250 km/h at first.
summary: The Ministry of Railways and the National High Speed Rail Corporation are preparing to switch on power for the Surat to Bilimora section of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train corridor on 20 November, the Indian Express reports. The 50-km elevated stretch has both up and down lines and uses a 2 x 25 kV overhead traction system. The railways aim to open the first section and start the corridor within ten months, with a target date of 15 August 2027 for India's first bullet train service.

The train itself, called the B28, is being built in India at BEML's Aditya plant in Bengaluru. The report says this route was chosen because of difficulties in getting rolling stock from Japan. The B28 is designed for 280 km/h but is expected to run at 250 km/h in the beginning. The full 508-km corridor will be powered from fourteen traction substations connected to the grid and run from a central control centre.

For residents of Bilimora and nearby towns, the practical point is safety. The high-speed rail corporation has warned residents, commuters and construction workers not to approach, touch or do any unauthorised work near the electrical installations, because the overhead wires will stay live all the time once energised.

The 15 August date is a target and the paper does not say how it will be met. Earlier timelines for the project have slipped, and the energisation of one section does not mean trains are ready to run.
